title: Stabilize kernel selection during capacity waves and tighten scheduler handoffs
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: During a capacity wave on 2026-02-26 we observed a sustained p95/p99 latency regression and >30% cost increase for several high-concurrency tenants. Root cause analysis points to non-deterministic kernel scoring plus interaction between speculative kernel probes and scheduler handoffs that amplified microbatch preemption and evictions. This ticket captures the short-term hardening, telemetry improvements, and medium-term changes required to prevent recurrence and enable safe rollouts.
root_cause_summary: A combination of (1) kernel scoring relying on noisy heuristics that drift when load composition changes, (2) speculative probe window widening during autoscaler bursts, and (3) scheduler handoff race where in-progress microbatches were being reassigned to marginal kernels, causing tail latency amplification and KV cache churn.
mitigation_summary: Immediate mitigations deployed: reduced speculative probe window by 40%, enforced microbatch lease extensions during handoffs, and reverted a recent heuristic that preferred 'fast-but-fragile' quant kernels under high concurrency. These mitigations dropped p95 by ~45% from peak and reduced eviction rate by ~60%.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a synthetic driver generating 3000 concurrent short-chat sessions (avg seq_len 64) with bursty peaks. 2) Apply the kernel-scoring feature flag with current heuristics. 3) Observe scheduler logs for probe events and microbatch reassignments. 4) Monitor p95/p99 and eviction counters over a 30-minute sustained burst.
action_items: Implement deterministic fallback ranking for kernel candidates (score seed + tie-breaker) - owner: Marco - estimate 3
Add a per-request 'handshake' trace that records kernel probe sequence, chosen kernel, and KV cache hit rate - owner: Priya Singh - estimate 2
Introduce a canary gating flag for heuristic changes that enforces a 24h steady-state window with telemetry pass criteria - owner: SRE team - estimate 2
Tighten probe window hysteresis to avoid probe amplification during autoscale spikes (configurable policy) - owner: Runtime - estimate 2
Expose microbatch lease metrics and alert when preemption rate > 2% for 10m - owner: Observability - estimate 1
Run a 72h soak using production-mirror traffic with the new deterministic ranking before enabling heuristics globally - owner: Platform - estimate 3
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for affected routes remains within 10% of baseline under a 30-minute synthetic capacity wave
Eviction rate and KV cache misses do not exceed historical baseline during the same test
All kernel changes gated behind canary flag and telemetry shows no regressions for 24h on mirrored traffic
Playbook steps documented and on-call runbook updated with rollback instructions

notes: Decision: short-term fixes acceptable while deterministic ranking and improved telemetry are implemented. We will not roll forward heuristic changes without canary gating. PR review required from Research, Runtime, and Observability before merging any kernel selection change.
risk_considerations: Changing kernel selection impacts cost and latency trade-offs; deterministic fallbacks reduce exploratory gains for potentially higher average cost but increase stability. Canary policy must be conservative to avoid wide blast radius.
cross_team_feedback: Product (Nadia Chen): Customers impacted in Dedicated tiers need clear comms. Proposed a status banner and targeted outreach for affected accounts.
Research (Dr. Omar Malik): Deterministic ranking should be validated against representative workloads; will provide benchmarking harness.
